context.why: The Account Center's overview is where a person arrives by default. A backend that contributes only navigation entries is discoverable to somebody already looking for it and nobody else. This story puts one card per installed backend on that overview, leading into that backend's pages. The navigation entries and the pages already exist and work.

spec_sections: User Story 3 - The overview says what is available
prior_decisions: D1 — every surface reads mvp_payments.namespaces.available_contributions() rather than asking apps.is_installed for itself.

D3 — availability is two questions and both already live on Contribution. is_available() asks the application registry. is_reachable() additionally asks whether the namespace's pages reverse, and the card is the caller that needs it: a card rendering a link through {% url %} raises NoReverseMatch and takes the whole overview down with it. Ask the object; do not re-derive either answer in the tag or the template.

D4 — mvp_payments precedes mvp in INSTALLED_APPS so that this package's copy of mvp/account/overview.html is found first and {% extends %} to the same name picks up django-mvp's. The demo and the test settings already have that order. Keeping {{ block.super }} is what lets several applications chain into the same block.

US-2's report raised one carry-forward: tests/test_app.py::TestNothingWithoutABackend asserts no card appears without the backend, and that assertion is currently vacuous because no card template exists. It boots a fresh process under tests.settings_without_backend rather than overriding INSTALLED_APPS, because the URL configuration and the navigation registration are both built once at process start and an override afterwards leaves both standing. Reuse that mechanism rather than inventing another.
context.conventions: CONSTITUTION.md Articles VIII (translatable strings), X (test structure), XI (a registered template tag module is an explicit exception to the cohesion rule), XVI (assert rendered output, never the presence of a class name). Cards on the overview are contributed by shipping a same-named template that extends mvp/account/overview.html and adds to its account.cards block through {{ block.super }} — django-mvp declares no attribute, no registry and no template tag for this.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given one available contribution, when the tag renders, then exactly one card is produced, carrying that namespace's heading and a link into its first page; given an unavailable contribution, when the tag renders, then it produces nothing for it.

Given the backend is installed, when a signed-in person opens the Account Center overview, then exactly one card for that backend is on it, leading into that backend's pages, and any card django-mvp or another application contributed is still there — the second half is what proves {{ block.super }} was kept.

Given a contribution that is available but whose pages do not reverse, when the tag renders, then it produces nothing for that contribution and the overview still renders. Ask Contribution.is_reachable(); do not re-implement the check.
Given the overridden overview template, when the Account Center overview renders, then the cards region contains both what django-mvp put there and this package's cards.

Given the README's description of what installing a backend produces, when it is read, then it names the card as well as the navigation entries, and states the INSTALLED_APPS order as a requirement rather than a suggestion. docs/namespaces.md already documents the card_template field; keep it true.

Carried forward from the previous story, which flagged it: its 'no card appears without the backend' assertion currently holds only because no card exists at all. Re-prove that absence against the real card markup — with the backend absent, the overview renders and this package's card is not on it — and say in your report how you established it.
